digest.component_or_area: ChatGPT agent workflow documentation and environment capability detection
propositions: ChatGPT sessions in connector-limited Rebar environments (missing local clone, Gerrit access, shell network access, or mounted tracker) lack guidance on recognizing the limitation, which operations remain safe, and when ticket creation cannot be completed natively.

The fallback mechanism for environments where native tracker access is impossible must produce a schema-conformant NDJSON payload (schema_version, agent-generated UUID4 ticket_id as provenance, ticket_type, title, status, description with Acceptance Criteria, optional parent_id) suitable for later review and import via rebar import, without falsely claiming persistence occurred.

The rebar import mechanism accepts NDJSON compiled-state projections (not raw event files), assigns fresh local ids and HLC timestamps, and is idempotent by source_id; in --dry-run mode, malformed records missing ticket_id or ticket_type are silently skipped with no counter increment and no warning, detectable only by comparing would_create + skipped against total record count.

Native ticket creation is impossible if and only if both the tracker-worktree dimension (no accessible tickets branch checkout) fails AND the network/remote dimension fails or the native rebar/rebar-mcp binary is unavailable; all other capability failures do not trigger the fallback and require explicit enumeration of remaining safe operations.

Hand-authoring, modifying, or deleting Rebar event files is unsafe due to the append-only concurrency model; the only sanctioned exceptional ingest path is rebar import (or rebar.import_tickets()), never raw Contents API writes to the tickets branch.

The GitHub repository is a read-only mirror; all code changes land through Gerrit; GitHub Issues are not a substitute for the Rebar tracker, and search-before-create with native tracker commands must be performed whenever the live tracker is accessible.
